Predicates:
CanRegister(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
ParticipateElection(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
CitizenshipUS(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
CitizenshipTaiwan(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
Official(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
Manager(x, y) ::: x is a manager at y.
HoldCitizenship(x, y) ::: x holds citizenship y.
Register(x) ::: x can register to vote.
VoteParticipation(x) ::: x participates in the election.
Manage(x, y) ::: x manages y.
Premises:
∀x (Register(x) → ParticipateElection(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote can participate in the election.
CitizenshipUS(x) → Register(x) ::: If someone has U.S. citizenship, then they can register to vote.
∀x (CitizenshipUS(x) ∨ CitizenshipTaiwan(x)) ::: Everyone has either U.S. or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬HoldCitizenship(x, RussianFederation) ::: No Russian Federation officials hold Taiwanese citizenship.
¬HoldCitizenship(Vladimir, Taiwanese) ∧ ¬Manage(Vladimir, Gazprom) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is he a manager at Gazprom.
Premises:
CanRegister(Ekaterina) ∨ Manage(Ekaterina, Gazprom) ::: Ekaterina can register to vote in the United States, or she is a Russian Federation official.
Conclusion:
CanRegister(Ekaterina) ∨ Manage(Ekaterina, Gazprom) ::: Ekaterina can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election or is a manager at Gazprom.
